# 0109. Leave a declared generated file out of the vocabulary advisory

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-10-17

## Context

The host's first search pass kept the exports its searches returned
under the folder the rulebook names for them, declared generated in the
attributes file as the family's rule requires, and the audit's
vocabulary advisory named thirty-three lines in them on every run, the
index's own abstracts carrying the words the prose law bans. The rule
had scoped a declared file out of the em dash count and the spelling
advisory alone, because those were the two checks that had met a
generated file when it was written, and the vocabulary advisory was left
reading machine output as if a person had written it.

## Options considered

- Dismiss the hits in every commit message that lands beside such a
  file. Refused, because an advisory that fires on every run on bytes
  nobody may edit is noise the law already excused, and a dismissal
  repeated is a rule left unwritten.
- Strip the abstracts from the exports. Refused, because the exports are
  kept so a disagreement can be re-read from the words the screen saw,
  and an export without its abstracts keeps the ids and loses the
  reason.

## Decision

A file declared `linguist-generated` in `.gitattributes` stands outside
the vocabulary advisory as it stands outside the em dash count and the
spelling advisory, in every seat's audit and in the root workflow's
prose step, and the shared prose law and the rules of conduct say so.
The selftest's declared plant carries a banned word beside its em dashes
and its invisible character, and must stay silent on both.

## Consequences

A generated file is read by no check of the prose law, and a pass that
keeps its exports lands without a dismissal for the words an index
returned.
